# Publishing monospace npm package:

## Good to know before you start

* `installer.js` **does not exist in the repository**. It is a build artifact: it is generated by the `bundle` script
  (esbuild bundle of `index.js`) and removed by `cleanup`. It only exists in the published tarball.
* `package.json` declares `"preinstall": "node installer.js"`, this is meant for people installing the published package.
  Running a plain `pnpm install` from a fresh checkout will therefore fail with `Cannot find module '.../installer.js'`.
* So in a fresh checkout, always install dependencies with scripts disabled:
  ```sh
  pnpm install --ignore-scripts
  ```
  If the bundle step later complains about the esbuild binary, run `pnpm rebuild esbuild`.
* Order matters: the `build` script is what creates `installer.js`, so don't try to run or test the installer before it.

## Release steps

* Install the dependencies (from a fresh checkout, see above):
  ```sh
  pnpm install --ignore-scripts
  ```
* First prepare the monospace release: 
  ```sh
  monospace run doc
  ```
* Check documentation and restore the logo in docs/monospace/cli/md/monospace.md
* Update package json version
  ```sh
  monospace run update-package-json -- --version=v0.0.XX
  ```
* Ensure all repositories are clean and git tag the monospace to the new version
* build the monospace release
  ```sh
  monospace run build
  ```
  it will run ```pnpm run build``` which will:
  * bump the package.json to the latest tag
  * update path to manifest files
  * clean the package directory
  * copy README.md, LICENSE, manifest files to the package folder
  * bundle the installer.js script
  * run npm pack (yes npm not pnpm as we will use npm publish and pnpm/npm behaves slightly differently when packing)

* Create new release on github and publish release files
* Check the package archive content (it must contain `installer.js`, `bin/*`, `README.md` and `man/*`)
* run ```npm publish --access public``` this will effectively publish the package to the npm registry
* once done you can run ```pnpm run cleanup``` to remove copied files (this also removes `installer.js`, which is why
  `pnpm install` without `--ignore-scripts` fails again afterwards)
